newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES MIXED IN HIGHER TURNOVER.
newsitem.headline: SHARES MIXED IN HIGHER TURNOVER.

text.p: Shares were mixed on Lithuania's bourse on Wednesday as a number of popular shares remained suspended, but brokers found reason for optimism in Hermis Bank and Baltic Shipyard.
"It was a little mixed but I'm still optimistic," said Saulius Merkys, a broker with Vilfima.
Central market turnover recovered somewhat, bouncing up to 618,000 litas from 192,000 litas.
Trade was mixed, with official list stocks rising 5.89 points to 931.56 points and group A shares losing 25.65 points to 1,943.96 points.
Hermis Bank shares advanced to 180.00 litas from 175.00 litas on central market turnover of 223,000 litas.
Brokers have been waiting for Hermis shares to rise following its positive results for the first four months of 1997.
Baltic Shipyard shares were lifted to 8.31 litas from 8.12 litas on central market turnover of 44,000 litas.
The rise came on the heels of an announcement that the government was planning to sell the state's 11.26 million litas stake on the bourse between June 7 and August 7.
Siauliai Bank saw 925,000 litas turnover in block trades at a price of 85.00 litas.

Deputy Chairman of Siauliai Bank Donatas Savickas told Reuters that there were two separate deals for Siauliai shares in block trades and that the bank's brokerage house had participated in one of the deals.
